the bone markers, osteocalcin and procollagen type 1 amino terminal propeptide (P1NP), have been shown to be significantly higher in children and adolescents during puberty and the reference intervals of these bone markers have been established for the first time in healthy South African children.
the reference intervals of the bone markers vary with age and gender and the reference intervals for vitamin D3 and PTH are abnormal in children who are obese or who use steroids.

bone marker levels are influenced by age, gender, puberty, BMI, and use of steroids.
reference intervals for all bone markers should be established in healthy children and adolescents, with a clear statement of the factors that may influence them.
the reference intervals for bone marker levels should be age and gender specific and should be determined in a large cohort of healthy individuals.

bone markers should be interpreted with caution in children with normal BMI z scores and in the absence of vitamin D(3)/PTH deficiency.
